bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the title page ("Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 2019. 51:189–215")
bibliography.note: Bouffard, D. & Wüest, A. 2019. Convection in lakes. Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics 51: 189–215 (Crossref gives issue 1). Matches the entry.

claims.claim: once the snow goes, sunlight through the ice drives radiative convection, deepening the mixed layer by about 0.5 m d⁻¹ and up to 3 m d⁻¹
claims.quote: CML-deepening rates of ∼0.5 m day−1 reaching up to 3 m day−1
claims.conditions: late winter, once snow has left the ice; 'up to 3 m day−1' only 'for strong solar radiation and weak background stratification'. The review relays these rates from Kirillin et al. (2012) and the plume velocities (w∗ ≈ 1–7 mm s−1) from Bouffard et al. (2016, Lake Onego)
claims.note: The primary source of the rates is Kirillin et al. 2012; the rewrite could cite 'Kirillin et al. 2012, via Bouffard & Wüest 2019'.

claims.claim: in a 3–5-m lake such convection would mix the whole column within 1–10 days (project estimate)
claims.quote: CML-deepening rates of ∼0.5 m day−1 reaching up to 3 m day−1
claims.conditions: inputs from the review; the arithmetic is the project's
claims.note: 3 m at 3 m/d = 1 d; 5 m at 0.5 m/d = 10 d. The span holds if the deepening rate stays constant to the bed; the review notes the layer deepens into background stratification, so the slow end is the more likely.

claims.location: p. 191 (PDF p. 3), Table 1, row w∗ (convective scale velocity)
claims.quote: w∗ (mm s−1) … Under ice: 1–7 … Free surface cooling: 1–50
claims.conditions: typical values; w∗ = (B∗ hCML)^1/3 (Deardorff 1970). 1–50 mm/s is for free-surface cooling; under ice 1–7 mm/s

claims.claim: convective velocities of 1–50 mm/s turn a few metres over in ~15–90 min
claims.source_value: the review gives no turnover time. The convective time scale h/w∗ for 2–5 m at 1–50 mm/s is ~40 s to ~83 min (3 m: 1–50 min); ~15–90 min holds only for w∗ ≈ 1–5 mm/s (the under-ice or weak-cooling end)
claims.location: p. 191 (PDF p. 3), Table 1; p. 194 (PDF p. 6), w∗ = (B∗hCML)^1/3
claims.conditions: project arithmetic on the review's w∗ range
claims.note: The chosen MIX_RATE (an e-fold of 30 min) lies inside the h/w∗ range, so the parameter can stand; the comment's '~15–90 min' should either say w∗ of a few mm/s or give '~1–80 min'.

notes: Only a code comment's arithmetic needs changing; the paper's own claim (§3.1.4) is confirmed. Other values in the review that the rewrite may use: temperature of maximum density TMD = 3.984 °C at the surface, TMD(z) ≈ 3.984 + 0.0021z (Table 1, p. 191); compensation depth zC ~0.1 m in a turbid lake (kd 1 m⁻¹) and ~0.5 m in a clear one (kd 0.2 m⁻¹) on a cold sunny day (p. 194); a thin stable diffusive layer separates the under-ice convective layer from the ice (p. 198, Fig. 4, Lake Onego); under-ice convection 'has been found to trigger early growth of phytoplankton' (p. 199, Vehmaa & Salonen 2009); differential heating between littoral and pelagic under ice can drive lake-wide gyres (p. 198, Kirillin et al.).
